claims.text: HEA multilayers with coherent interfaces can serve as a transition material between diffusion-mediated and dislocation-mediated creep.
Controlled introduction of interface coherency can produce HEA multilayers with coherent interfaces.
Interface coherency mediates a transition from diffusion-mediated creep to dislocation-mediated creep.
Introducing coherent interfaces improves the creep resistance of HEA multilayers relative to incoherent-interface HEA multilayers.
The proposed creep-mechanism transition is relevant under high-temperature and high-stress conditions.
Temperature and stress thresholds exist beyond which interface coherency no longer influences creep behavior.
The specific role of interface coherency in the creep behavior of HEA multilayers is not well understood.
